clue.text: Rabbit maybe that's going nuclear?

definitions.meaning: rabbits famously multiply quickly, so one is an animal that produces young at speed
a reactor of this type makes more fissile fuel than it burns, a kind of nuclear power plant

explanation.surface: A joke that a prolific rabbit has gone atomic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a prolific animal and a reactor that generates more fuel than it consumes.

clue.text: Form of life, see, captured by female artist

indicators.note: the female and artist pieces surround the word for see

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A woman painter has caught a sight of some life form.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant life of a region is a kind of life, distinct from the animal kind.

clue.text: Little man, after act of undressing, streaked

indicators.note: the little man is placed after the act of undressing

parts.note: a strip is an act of taking off clothes
Ed is a short form of Edward, a little name for a man

explanation.surface: A small man after a striptease has streaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streaked' looks like running naked, fitting the undressing, but it means marked with lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked with bands or lines of colour, as a zebra is, the answer describes something with stripes.

clue.text: Boar and moll possibly in this tactile activity for two?

definitions.text: Boar and moll possibly in this tactile activity for two?

parts.words: Boar and moll possibly in this tactile activity for two?
parts.note: the letters of boar and moll appear jumbled inside the phrase, and the phrase names couples holding each other while stepping to music

explanation.surface: A pig and a gangster's girlfriend take part in a touchy-feely pastime for couples.
explanation.walkthrough: Boar and moll rearranged are all in the answer, with CING left over; the rest of the clue describes partners holding each other on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples hold each other in formal steps like the waltz, a hands-on pastime for pairs.

clue.text: A retreating Nell, damaged in complex love network

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl called Nell, hurt, withdraws from a tangled romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Three people romantically entangled with each other form a complicated set of relationships.

clue.text: Daughter came down exhausted

parts.note: rain came down, so it rained

explanation.surface: A daughter came downstairs worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling emptied of all energy is being tired out.

clue.text: What you may get with chemicals ruining nice roast

definitions.text: What you may get with chemicals

indicators.note: ruining means spoiling, so the letters of the following words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Chemicals added to a lovely roast joint spoil it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing chemicals produces chemical changes, the processes chemists study.

clue.text: Shoe old bird outside cricket club? Shame!

indicators.note: the old bird surrounds the club letters

parts.note: the moa was an extinct flightless bird of New Zealand
sin can mean a shame, as in it's a sin

explanation.surface: An extinct bird wearing a shoe at a cricket ground: how shameful.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft leather slip-on of Native American origin is a type of shoe.

clue.text: The male politician supplying drug

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A male politician is caught supplying narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis comes from this plant, so it names a narcotic.

clue.text: Aroma with yours and my party being held

indicators.note: the party is held within the word for yours and my, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: yours and mine together is ours, the possessive OUR
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A smell hangs about at a party we are hosting.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a smell, and odour is the general word for a smell.

clue.text: Drunk askew with ale — one embedded can't drop off

indicators.note: the letter for one is set into the middle of the jumbled letters
drunk means muddled, so the letters of the words that follow are jumbled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who drank ale and is lying askew cannot get to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' fits the surface's drinker, but it signals the shuffle that gives LESAWAKE; 'drop off' means fall asleep, not fall down.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie awake is to stay in bed unable to fall asleep, which is being unable to nod off.

clue.text: Agent's friend caught on the rebound — an enthusiastic type

indicators.note: bouncing back, so the string of pieces is read from right to left

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent; the 's just joins
a pal is a friend
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An agent's pal has been caught on the rebound after a breakup, and is keen.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applauds keenly shows enthusiasm, so the word suits an eager supporter.

clue.text: Not work to keep partners at table 24/7?

indicators.note: the words for not and work hold the partners inside them

parts.note: taken as written
North and South are partners at the bridge table, NS
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A bridge pair is told not to stop playing all day and night.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; North and South play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Round the clock, twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week, means without a break.

clue.text: Sort of appeal to boy to deliver food container

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
a lad is a boy
in cricket the bowler delivers the ball, so to bowl is to deliver

explanation.surface: A plea to a boy to bring round something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: BOWL is what a cricket bowler does when delivering the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide serving dish for leaves and dressing is a vessel that holds food.

clue.text: Happy marriage for couple? Falling out could make them vocal

indicators.note: a falling out is a quarrel, here signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A happy couple who row could become loud about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage made out of romance rather than convenience is a union for affection.

clue.text: In bed start to read rubbish

indicators.note: the first letter of read goes inside the word for bed

parts.note: a doss is a makeshift bed, as in a doss-house

indicators.note: the start of the word read is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Lying in bed, someone starts to read some trash.
explanation.walkthrough: A doss-house is a cheap lodging house, and a doss is a bed there.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste or worthless matter, the scum of melted metal, hence trash.

clue.text: Pound lost — keen person in no danger of looking fat!

definitions.text: person in no danger of looking fat

indicators.note: to pound is to batter, so the letters of the words after it are broken up

explanation.surface: A dieter who has lost a pound is keen, being nowhere near fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like weight lost, but it is the instruction to scramble LOST and KEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone painfully thin is described as a bag of bones, the frame of the body.

clue.text: Man has penned very short book

indicators.note: the man's name encloses the short form, as if it were penned in

parts.note: Noel is a man's name
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A man has written a very short book.
explanation.definitionFit: A long prose fiction published as a volume is a kind of book.

clue.text: Lengthen the disillusionment

definitions.meaning: to drop a hem lower makes a garment longer

explanation.definitionFit: Dropping a hem makes it longer, and as a noun the phrase means a disappointment.

clue.text: What's disastrous about one essential matter being controlled by state

indicators.note: the word for disastrous goes around the other pieces

parts.note: something dire is disastrous
I is the Roman numeral one
the gist is the essential point

explanation.surface: A disastrous situation centred on one key issue under state control.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigiste economy is one run by central government direction, so it is state-directed.

clue.text: Relation making good money abroad before remuneration's cut

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the word for remuneration loses its last letter

parts.note: pay is remuneration; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A relative earns good money overseas before his pay is reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandfather is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Pom batting to get one century after another?

definitions.text: Pom batting to get one century after another?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

indicators.note: batting about means knocking around, so the letters of the short word are mixed up

parts.note: a ton is a century of runs in cricket, so it is another century

explanation.surface: An English batsman scoring hundred after hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Denis Compton was an English batsman who scored many centuries; Pom is Australian slang for an English person, and ton is cricket slang for a hundred runs.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the prolific English batsman Denis Compton, a Pom piling up hundreds.

clue.text: Gosh, any number will be needed to get crop!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how many are needed for a harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal grain such as wheat or maize is grown as a farm crop.

clue.text: Sailor on desert island? Sea food must be found

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
someone on a desert island is by themselves, alone

explanation.surface: A castaway sailor must forage for seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible sea snail, also called ormer or paua, is eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Unit formerly deployed to protect leader of Uruguay

indicators.note: the word for formerly goes around and shields the letter

parts.note: once means formerly, at one time

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An old military unit sent to guard the leader of Uruguay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit formerly' reads as a former army unit, but the definition is just 'Unit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixteenth of a pound, it is a unit of weight.

clue.text: Wartime activity number one about to be embraced by seaman

indicators.note: the seaman wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a rating is a sailor below officer rank
I is oneself, number one
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A sailor clutches his own interests during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Limiting food and fuel to fixed shares was a familiar measure in Britain during both world wars.

clue.text: Wild dog (must be kept outside home!)

definitions.text: Wild dog (must be kept outside home!)

indicators.note: the scrambled dog sits outside the word for home, enclosing it
wild means unruly, so the letters of dog are scrambled

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A warning that a feral dog should never be let into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the mixed-up DGO is kept outside, wrapped around the home letters, just as a wild dog stays out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian wild dog is a feral canine that no one keeps indoors.

clue.text: It's explosive — with terrible danger when it goes off being held!

definitions.text: It's explosive — with terrible danger when it goes off being held!

indicators.note: the abbreviation for explosive holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: HE is high explosive
and means with, in addition to

indicators.note: terrible means awful, so the letters of danger are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning about a bomb that is dangerous when it detonates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' gives GRENAD; HE (high explosive) is a standard crossword abbreviation, and the whole clue also describes the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bomb thrown by hand, it is an explosive device that is dangerous when detonated.
